subject: Heimdall integration: SDK auth, routing & observability hooks
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@heimdall.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-28T16:00:00Z
Subject: Initial discovery notes: SDK auth & telemetry

Soojin / team — great walkthrough today, thanks. I wanted to capture a few of the technical asks that came up from our infra and observability teams so we can align on next steps: 

- Auth: Heimdall supports OIDC (internal IdP), mTLS between our edge and external providers, and long-lived API keys for service accounts. Primary ask: can Redwood SDK support short-lived OIDC tokens and also an mTLS option for our on-prem connectors?
- Routing/variants: we need the ability to route requests to a primary model and a cheaper fallback variant when under load (or to the reranker pipeline). Any config examples would help.
- Structured output / tool calling: we use a tool-calling pattern; need clear examples for schema/validation and best-effort parsing from Redwood responses.
- Embeddings/reranker: we plan to compute 384-dim embeddings and do a light re-rank step. Can Redwood host a reranker endpoint or recommend best practice for batching and latency?
- Observability: critical ask — full trace propagation across Heimdall -> Redwood -> our downstream services. We need a stable correlation header (we prefer X-Request-ID) and a per-request latency breakdown header (per-token vs model vs network). Also a minimal list of log fields to include for our ingestion (request_id, trace_id, model_variant, kv_cache_hit, latency_ms).

I attached our infra outline (heimdall-infra-outline.pdf) — that shows the edge, service mesh, and where we want trace handoff.

High level ask: can you send a short integration plan with owners, a recommended auth approach, and the specific observability fields/headers your SDK will emit?

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Engineering
Heimdall Analytics

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@heimdall.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T16:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial discovery notes: SDK auth & telemetry

Alex — thanks for the clear notes and the infra outline. Recap below + proposed plan (short, tactical items first). Attaching: redwood-sdk-auth-guide.pdf and observability-hooks-proposal.md.

Recap / recommendations
- Auth: recommend OIDC with short-lived access tokens (1–15m) + automatic refresh in the SDK. For on-prem connectors we support mTLS as an opt-in transport layer. API keys are supported for service accounts but we don’t recommend long-lived keys for production. (See redwood-sdk-auth-guide.pdf)
- Routing: Redwood supports policy-based routing by header or by weight. Example policy: route by client_header (X-Redwood-Route) with fallback to model_variant: gpt-small -> gpt-medium -> reranker. We can also do latency-based fallbacks. I’ll include a sample config snippet in the doc.
- Structured output / tool calling: we emit structured JSON + optional validation errors in the response envelope. Example: a top-level "tool_calls" array plus an "__raw_text" field. We recommend a strict JSON schema for tool responses; the SDK includes a helper to validate and reattempt.
- Embeddings & reranker: recommend batching embedding requests at 64/128 vectors depending on length; host reranker as a lightweight HTTP endpoint behind Redwood or call your internal reranker using the embedding vectors returned. For 384-dim we expect ~6–12ms per vector on our quantized endpoints; batching helps.
- Observability hooks (concrete):
  - Correlation headers accepted: X-Request-ID (preferred by Heimdall) + W3C traceparent. Redwood will propagate incoming X-Request-ID and attach X-Redwood-Trace (internal trace id).
  - Latency header: X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown: token_ms=model:12, network_ms=3, total_ms=15
  - Logging fields we will emit (structured JSON): [request_id, trace_id, user_id|null, model, model_variant, kv_cache_hit, batch_size, token_count, latency_ms, rerank_score?].
  - Sampling & dashboards: Redwood Console can ingest traces at 100% for errors and sampled at 5–10% for success traces. We'll share a dashboard template (attached) with the key panels: per-route p50/p95, KV cache hit rate, average tokens per request, embedding batch throughput.

Proposed next steps (owners & ETA):
1) Share canonical headers and sample requests — Soojin (today) — done (attached proposal).
2) Provide SDK config snippet + canary rollout plan — Jonas (2 business days)
3) Heimdall shares final arch diagram and preferred auth mode (OIDC vs mTLS) — Alex (EOD Thu)
4) Engineer pairing session for initial integration (30–60m) — schedule next week; propose Wed 2027-07-07 10:00 PT.

Open questions:
- Do you require HSM/KMS integration on token issuance? If yes we’ll involve our security team.
- For reranker hosting — do you want Redwood to host the reranker inside your project or call out to Heimdall endpoints? Each has tradeoffs (latency vs control).

If this aligns I’ll circulate the sample config and a canary template.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood-sdk-auth-guide.pdf (recommended auth flows, code snippets)
- observability-hooks-proposal.md (header examples, logging fields, dashboard links)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@heimdall.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T23:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial discovery notes: SDK auth & telemetry

Adding a couple of pragmatic suggestions from the infra side: 

- Canary / rollout: include a reranker threshold and a header to opt-in experimental reranker (X-Redwood-Canary: rerank-v1). That lets you toggle without config deploys.
- Reranker thresholds: recommend a soft threshold (score delta) for applying rerank to avoid churn; we can provide a default (0.08) and a tuning dashboard.
- Ephemeral creds: for SDKs running on Heimdall connectors, using short-lived creds emitted by your token service reduces risk; Redwood SDKs support ephemeral token refresh hooks.

I’ll add a sample canary JSON and a Dashboard link to the observability doc Soojin attached. Happy to pair on the canary config during the scheduled integration session.

—Jonas
Engineering Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference

> On 2027-06-29 16:12, Soojin Lee wrote:
> > Alex — thanks for the clear notes and the infra outline. Recap below + proposed plan...

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@heimdall.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T18:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial discovery notes: SDK auth & telemetry

This looks great — thanks for the concrete plan and attachments. Quick answers and next actions: 

- Auth: we’ll proceed with OIDC short-lived tokens for hosted connectors and mTLS for our on-prem collectors. I’ll confirm if we need KMS/HSM by Friday.
- Reranker: we prefer Redwood to host a lightweight reranker behind the same call chain for lower latency. Please include the hosting/cost estimate in your follow-up.
- Observability: X-Request-ID and W3C traceparent propagation is acceptable. The X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown header will satisfy our latency SLA checks.

I opened OPS-731 in Jira for the integration work (https://heimdall.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-731). I’ll share our architecture diagram (heimdall-arch-diagram.vsdx) before EOD tomorrow.

Can we target a 2-week canary starting 2027-07-05? If Redwood can provide the canary template and the console dashboard share-link we can kick off the pairing session next week. Also please send the HubSpot deal link and a short SOW estimate for the reranker hosting.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Engineering
Heimdall Analytics
